overlooked_assumption: The code assumes `end` is not February 29 of a leap year when computing `start = end.replace(year=end.year - 5)`, so subtracting 5 years from February 29 lands on a non-existent date (e.g., February 29, 2024 minus 5 years → February 29, 2019 is valid, but if the original date was February 29 of a leap year and the subtraction crosses a non-leap-year boundary or the date arithmetic is naive, it can produce an invalid date like February 30 or February 29 in a non-leap year).
why_it_breaks: When `end` is February 29 of a leap year (e.g., 2024), calling `end.replace(year=end.year - 5)` attempts to create February 29 of the target year. If the target year is not a leap year, Python raises `ValueError: day is out of range for month`. The agent assumed the date arithmetic would always produce a valid date, ignoring the leap-year edge case where the day 29 does not exist in the resulting year.
